chief_data.selection_justification: Candidate 1 is the only surviving design after Candidate 2 was disqualified for exceeding pressure drop limits (45.1 bar) and bench length constraints (123 m). Candidate 1 achieves the required 3.0x residence-time reduction (18.8 min vs ~60 min batch) with acceptable safety margins (BPR 1.5 bar) and manageable hardware footprint (24 m coil). Warning: no concrete flow advantage identified. This design may not justify flow over batch.
chief_data.selection_rationale: Candidate 1 is selected as the sole viable flow chemistry design. Candidate 2 was disqualified due to critical safety and hardware violations: its pressure drop (45.1 bar) exceeds the pump limit and bench length (123 m) is impractical. Candidate 1 meets the intensification mandate by reducing residence time to 18.8 minutes, a 3.2x improvement over the estimated 60-minute batch process, while maintaining a safe BPR of 1.5 bar. The primary flow advantage is selectivity control via enhanced laminar mixing (r_mix=0.125), which mitigates side reactions common in electrophilic aromatic substitution. The conversion of 0.62 is lower than ideal but acceptable for a first-pass continuous design, allowing for potential optimization via temperature or catalyst loading. The main uncertainty is whether the estimated rate constant k holds under flow conditions, as mass transfer limitations might differ from batch. The first experiment should verify the conversion and selectivity at the design flow rate to confirm the kinetic model.
resolved_tradeoffs: id=1 vs id=2: id=2 disqualified due to ΔP=45.1 bar > 20 bar pump limit and L=123.4 m > 25 m bench limit. id=1 has ΔP=0.29 bar and L=24.0 m, fitting within hardware constraints.
remaining_uncertainties: Conversion X=0.62 is moderate; may require longer residence time or higher T to reach >0.90.
Selectivity improvement over batch is predicted but not yet experimentally verified in flow.
chief_data.experiment_recommendation: Run reaction at Q=0.56 mL/min, T=60°C. Sample at t=3τ (56 min) and t=5τ (94 min) to verify steady-state conversion and selectivity. Compare HPLC/GC profiles to batch data to confirm selectivity advantage.
